origin.description: ASCII input is reported as ASCII with confidence 1. Other input uses stringi and keeps encodings above the threshold.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

origin.details: ASCII input is reported as ASCII with confidence 1. Other input uses stringi and keeps encodings above the threshold.
origin.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
origin.example:
guessed <- guess_encoding(readr_example("mtcars.csv"))
paste(paste(guessed$encoding, sprintf("%.17g", guessed$confidence), sep = "="), collapse = ",")

translation.description: ASCII input is reported as ASCII with confidence 1. Other input uses stringi and keeps encodings above the threshold.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

translation.details: ASCII input is reported as ASCII with confidence 1. Other input uses stringi and keeps encodings above the threshold.
translation.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
translation.example:
guessed = guess_encoding(readr_example("mtcars.csv"))
return ",".join(encoding + "=" + format(confidence, ".17g") for encoding, confidence in zip(guessed.columns[0], guessed.columns[1]))
